title: Porter's five forces
caption: Four forces press on the rivalry between existing competitors in the middle. The stronger each force, the lower the industry's average profit. Each arm says what makes that force strong.
alt: Rivalry among existing competitors in the centre with arrows from threat of new entrants (above), threat of substitutes (below), bargaining power of suppliers (left) and bargaining power of buyers (right).
description: Centre: rivalry among existing competitors, high when competitors are many and similar, growth is slow or fixed costs are high.
Above: threat of new entrants, high when barriers to entry are low.
Left: bargaining power of suppliers, high when suppliers are few or switching costs are high.
Right: bargaining power of buyers, high when buyers are few and large and switching is cheap.
Below: threat of substitutes, high when other products meet the same need at good value.

centre.label: Rivalry among existing competitors
centre.note: many similar rivals, slow growth, high fixed costs

arms.label: Threat of new entrants
arms.note: strong when barriers to entry are low

arms.label: Bargaining power of suppliers
arms.note: strong when suppliers are few or switching costs high

arms.label: Bargaining power of buyers
arms.note: strong when buyers are few, large and can switch cheaply

arms.label: Threat of substitutes
arms.note: strong when other products meet the same need
